trĭnundĭnus , a, um, adj. tres nundinae,
I.of or belonging to three weekly market-days (very rare): “trinundino die,” after seventeen days, Macr. S. 1, 16, 34 ; v. trinus, II. B., and nundinus, III. — Hence, adv.: trĭnundĭnō , = trinundino die, Macr. S. 2, 13, 7.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
